prompt.context: Our client is Hudson Electronics, a manufacturer of high-tech electronic devices based in the US. They have just developed a new product called the Optic-Eye. This is an augmented reality tool that users wear around their eyes. This product is new to the market and needs WiFi to work, but also could potentially be bundled with a cellular service provider. The way that it could be sold is similar to how cell phones are currently sold, in an annual contract.
prompt.question: Our client is debating between partnering with Verizon/ATT vs. partnering with other providers, but is unsure of which of these two options will work best. Which partnership option should Hudson Electronics choose?

clarifying_info.q: What are the 'Other' providers in the alternative option?
clarifying_info.a: There are 6 national level carriers: Sprint, T-Mobile, U.S. Cellular, Cricket, Boost Mobile, and MetroPCS.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue target or success metric for this decision?
clarifying_info.a: The objective is to achieve $1B in revenue in 2 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the contract price for each option?
clarifying_info.a: The contract price for Verizon/ATT is $400, and for Others is $500.

exhibits.title: Customer Base
exhibits.shows: A table listing wireless data service providers and their current customer base in the US. Total US market is ~50M consumer wireless data service customers.

exhibits.title: Customer Feedback
exhibits.shows: A comparison chart of customer preferences for ATT/Verizon vs. Other carriers, listing what each group prioritizes.

exhibits.title: Stores Per Company
exhibits.shows: A table showing number of US retail stores and non-US retail stores for each wireless data service provider.

framework: Market Structure: size of the market through each set of providers, national and regional reach, competitors in the space
Customer Preferences: customer profile (demographic, income differences), willingness to pay for this type of product, preference for new technology
Channels: online vs. in-store format, national footprint, distribution channels
Risks: market power of the providers, regulatory risks with consumer electronics, customer perception

questions.prompt: What is the market size of each telecom provider, and how many customers do we need to fulfill the $1B revenue target?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that the combined ATT+Verizon market (20M) is smaller than the Other market (30M) by 33%. Candidate should calculate the number of customers needed to hit $1B for each option, then compare feasibility.

math.setup: Revenue target = $1B. Contract price for ATT/Verizon = $400 per customer. Contract price for Others = $500 per customer. Calculate customers needed for each option.
math.answer: Hudson needs 2.5M customers from the ATT/Verizon pool (12.5% of 20M) or 2M customers from the Other pool (6.7% of 30M). On a pure penetration-rate basis, Other carriers require a lower share, but candidate should recognize that willingness to adopt new tech matters more than raw market size.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between each type of customer, and how will their preferences drive adoption of this new augmented reality product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 to contrast the two segments. ATT/Verizon customers prioritize quality, brand, and speed — they are less price-sensitive and more likely to try premium new technology. Other carrier customers prioritize price and contract terms, making them far harder to convert for a new, unproven AR device. Candidate should conclude that ATT/Verizon customers are more promising targets for Optic-Eye adoption.

questions.prompt: How will Hudson Electronics reach and sell to the most promising customers?
questions.guidance: Candidate should focus on US stores only (product is US-based). ATT has 2,200 US retail stores and Verizon has 1,800, for a combined 4,000 stores. Other carriers have 3,000 US stores total but spread across 6 carriers. ATT alone has more US retail locations than the entire Other carrier group. Candidate should note that a wider, more concentrated US retail presence makes it easier to demonstrate and sell a novel AR product in-store.

math.setup: Compare US retail store counts for each option.
steps: ATT alone (2,200) > entire Other carrier group (3,000 across 6 carriers)
math.answer: ATT/Verizon offers 4,000 combined US retail locations vs. 3,000 for all Other carriers combined, providing a broader and more concentrated US distribution network.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors would you consider in making the decision on a telecom provider?

categories.name: Market Structure
ideas: Size of market through each set of providers
Competitive landscape within each provider's ecosystem

categories.name: Customer Preferences
ideas: Willingness to pay for this type of premium product
Preference for and openness to new technology

categories.name: Channels
ideas: Online vs. in-store format for product demonstration

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Market power and negotiating leverage of the providers
Customer perception of a new, unproven AR device

recommendation: Hudson Electronics should partner with ATT and Verizon rather than with the Other carriers.

The combined ATT/Verizon market of 20M customers, while smaller in size, consists of less price-sensitive, quality-focused customers who are more likely to adopt a premium new technology product like Optic-Eye. ATT/Verizon also offers a wider combined US retail presence (4,000 stores) for in-store demonstration and sales.
risks: Regulatory risks around a new consumer electronics product entering the market
The quality of the product itself and whether it will perform as advertised, which could damage the ATT/Verizon partnership if reception is poor
next_steps: Conduct deeper analysis into the percentage of ATT/Verizon customers who will actually purchase Optic-Eye to stress-test the $1B revenue target
Understand the contracting process end-to-end with ATT and Verizon to assess deal terms and time-to-market
